sources.text: Git records project snapshots in commits. Ordinary new commits preserve earlier history. Saving a file in an editor does not itself make a Git commit.

output.draft: Git keeps selected versions of a project as commits.

output.answer: Git is a tool that keeps selected versions of a project so you can inspect an earlier version or restore its file contents later. Saving a file in your editor does not make a commit, and Git does not automatically record every edit.
